newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Council agrees to projects on out-of-court settlements.
newsitem.headline: Council agrees to projects on out-of-court settlements.

text.p: The Consumer Council agreed on Tuesday that a number of pilot projects should be set up to see how consumers could gain redress in cross-border disputes without going through court.

Pointing to the cost of court action, Ireland's Consumer Affairs Minister Pat Rabbitte told a news conference the move to out of court settlements would provide an "informal and speedy" way to address complaints.

"Independent research has shown the average cost of in-court settlement of a transfrontier EU case concerning a dispute worth Ecus 2,000 is in fact 2,500 and can take an average of two years," he said in a statement.

The difficulty of pursuing cross-border complaints is seen as hampering the credibility of the single market. How are people going to have the confidence to buy goods and services if they have no guarantee of their consumer rights?
The move to set up pilot projects came during a discussion on the Commission's Communication on an action plan on consumer access to justice and the settlement of consumer disputes.

Rabbitte also said that substantial progress had been made during an orientation debate on the draft directive on injunctions for the protection of consumer interests, although in the absence of the European Palriament's opinion a formal agreement was not possible.
Rabbitte said that additional technical work would be necessary and that final adoption could take place during the Dutch presidency.
Under that directive designated national organisations would take up individual consumer complaints.
